title: OKR-mapped priority funnels with cost-elasticity scoring
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Our current RICE-based playbooks surface high-impact, low-effort items, but they treat cost and latency as separate knobs. This leads to inconsistent prioritization for initiatives that materially change serving economics (eg. batching, KV cache improvements, quantization).

Goal: Create a reproducible, OKR-aligned prioritization funnel that: 1) maps candidate initiatives to explicit OKRs/initiatives, 2) scores them using a RICE-derivative that folds in expected unit-cost delta and latency SLO risk, and 3) yields a small set of candidate items per cycle with recommended rollout patterns (canary, limited-burst, dedicated reserve) and operational checkpoints.

Key idea: Replace a single scalar "Effort" with a two-dimensional cost-effort view and an elasticity multiplier that discounts high-cost-reduction work that has multiplicative long-term impact. The funnel tiers: 1) OKR Mapping, 2) Quantified Impact & Cost Delta, 3) Confidence & Risk Adjustments, 4) Operational Readiness & Rollout Plan.

This ticket scopes the model, scoring formula, example scoring sheet, and a lightweight rubric for selecting a pilot set of 6 items for the next cycle.
scoring_model: Base RICE variant: Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. New model: Score_ce = ((Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort) * ElasticityMultiplier * SLOAdjustment. Where: ElasticityMultiplier = 1 + CostElasticityCoefficient * (ExpectedUnitCostReduction / BaseUnitCost). SLOAdjustment = 1 - RiskWeight * ExpectedLatencySLOIncreaseFraction. Intuition: initiatives that reduce per-token cost at scale get a multiplicative boost; initiatives that risk SLOs are penalized. All inputs normalized to 0-100 before computation.
acceptance_criteria: Documented formula with worked examples that can be reproduced in the Roadmap spreadsheet (Google Drive link included)
Rubric for translating OKRs to "reach" buckets (guidelines for users and product metrics owner)
Pilot set of 4-6 initiatives scored and prioritized for 2026-Q2 with assigned owners and rollout recommendations
A short README and a one-slide summary for the exec roadmap sync

notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Multiplicative elasticity rewards large-scale cost wins but can over-index on backend-only improvements that have low product-visible impact. Mitigation: cap ElasticityMultiplier at 3x and require product owner sign-off for backend-only items.

Tradeoff: Normalizing reach is subjective across teams; standardization requires metadata from analytics and product metric owners. Short-term: use conservative buckets and require metric owner validation.

Operational cost: Scoring requires an estimate of unit-cost delta which adds estimation burden; recommend pairing PMs with an "econ reviewer" from Finance/Runtime team for scoring in planning ceremonies.
